subject: Incident update: confirmation of no customer data exposure
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jade Li <jade.li@securepay.com>, SecurePay Security <secops@securepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Incident: abnormal worker restarts — initial note

Hi Jade / SecurePay secops team,

We observed a period of abnormal worker restarts in our inference pool this morning that affected some request routing for a subset of tenant traffic. Our on-call has queued a full trace and we’re treating this as a high-priority operational incident. At this stage we have no evidence of data leakage, but we wanted to notify you proactively and will share findings as soon as we have them.

What we’re doing now:
- Collecting process and audit logs across impacted hosts
- Freezing relevant runbooks and persisting KV cache snapshots
- Preserving network flow logs and S3 access logs for a full forensics window

We expect a preliminary update within 24 hours. Please let us know if you require any specific exports.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Incident: abnormal worker restarts — preliminary findings

Hi Jade — quick update from the forensic team.

Summary (prelim):
- Root cause: a scheduler bug triggered a race with our autoscaler that resulted in repeated worker restarts for a small shard of the pool.
- Scope: approx. 0.4% of requests routed to the affected shard between 08:42–09:10 PST.
- Customer data handling: all inference requests were processed in-memory; persistent storage writes were not triggered by the failing job.

Log checks performed so far:
- Application request traces: verified request IDs and session IDs; no anomalous outbound connections observed
- S3 access logs: no PutObject/Write operations correlated with affected worker host IDs
- Access tokens: no usage outside expected vectors

We’re attaching a small package with log snippets and hash summaries for your review. The team is still completing a deeper audit (credentials, telemetry exfil vectors, host memory snapshots). Will share the full integrity summary in the next 24 hours.

Short ask: can you confirm whether you want us to run an expanded export of request-level payloads for your security team? We can produce a redacted copy that omits PII if preferred.

—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Final integrity check and forensics summary

On Thu, 03 Dec 2026 at 14:22:00 -0800 Marissa Cole wrote:
> Hi Jade — quick update from the forensic team.
>
> Summary (prelim):
> - Root cause: a scheduler bug triggered a race with our autoscaler that resulted in repeated worker restarts for a small shard of the pool.
> - Scope: approx. 0.4% of requests routed to the affected shard between 08:42–09:10 PST.
> - Customer data handling: all inference requests were processed in-memory; persistent storage writes were not triggered by the failing job.

Thanks — following up with the completed deeper audit. Below are the concrete checks we ran and the outcomes.

Forensics checklist (completed 04 Dec 2026):
1) Host memory snapshots
   - Collected and hashed; no artifacts indicating staged payloads or staged dumps on disk. Hashes were compared against our baseline snapshots for the last 30 days.
2) Network egress and NAT logs
   - Reviewed firewall egress rules and NAT connection logs; no large data transfers correlated with affected hosts. Mean bytes/connection consistent with control period.
3) S3/Object store audit
   - Cross-referenced PutObject events and multipart uploads; zero writes from the affected host IDs during incident window.
4) Token and key usage
   - Checked KMS access logs; internal keys used only by authorized control plane services, no anomalous decryption requests.
5) KV cache persistence
   - KV caches are ephemeral for these workers; snapshots were verified and no unexpected persists were observed.
6) Application-level request validation
   - Request payload sampling (redacted) matched expected schemas; no suspicious field exfil patterns.

Conclusion: Based on the checks above, we have no evidence of customer data loss or exfiltration. We are classifying this as an operational integrity incident with no privacy breach.

Next steps we completed for mitigation:
- Scheduler patch deployed to prevent the specific race condition
- Host-level egress monitoring threshold raised and alerting tuned
- 72-hour extended log retention for the affected shard window for additional oversight

If you want, we can produce a signed integrity statement and provide the raw hash manifests for independent verification.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Forensics & Security, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Final confirmation — no customer data loss or exfiltration detected

Hi Jade / SecurePay team,

Following the forensics runbook and the independent review request from Auditus, this is our formal confirmation:

- Outcome: No evidence of customer data loss, staged exfiltration, or unauthorized persistent writes was found after exhaustive checks across host memory, network egress, S3 logs, token/KMS usage, and application traces.
- Evidence provided: integrity_audit_summary_20261204.pdf (hash manifests), securepay_log_snippets_20261203.zip (log excerpts), and the canonical verification steps provided to Auditus.
- Retention: we have set a 90-day preserved window for the affected logs and will provide access to Auditus under an NDA as requested.

We realize any incident is disruptive, and we appreciate your patience. If SecurePay would like a signed attestation on company letterhead, we can generate and deliver that within 48 hours.

Please confirm receipt and whether you need the redacted request-level export for additional assurance.

Best,
Markus Klein
